Application Materials.content:
Please complete the application form accordingly and attach photocopies of the documents as instructed. Your application will only be processed when all documents and payment have been received.
Official/Certified true copies of transcripts and photocopies of required documents can be delivered either by hand or by mail to: MAE Programme Office, School of Economics, Singapore Management University, 90 Stamford Road, Singapore 178903.
Please submit copies of the following documents:
- Identity Card (For Singapore Citizens/PR)
- Passport & Identity Card (For non-Singapore Citizens)
- GMAT/GRE/SMU Admissions Test Official Score Report
- TOEFL/IELTS English Proficiency Examination Result (for applicants whose first language is not English)
- Bachelor Degree Certificate
- Official Transcripts of Bachelor’s Degree
- Master’s Degree Certificate (if applicable)
- Official Transcripts of Master’s Degree (if applicable)
- Current resume
- Two Referee Reports
- Personal Statement
- Any other supporting documents

Academic Requirements.content:
- **Good Bachelor's degree**.
- Effective August 2026 intake: the August intake will be open to students from diverse academic backgrounds. **Foundation courses will be provided to bridge any knowledge gaps**. Students with strong quantitative backgrounds may be exempted from these courses and complete the programme in 12 months.
- The MSE includes an entry pathway for students without prior training in economics; the programme has a pathway for non-Econ majors.
- Foundations are intended for students from non-Economics backgrounds who do not have the necessary training in economic theory and advanced quantitative techniques required by the MSE. Students with strong economics knowledge and advanced quantitative techniques are exempted from this component.
- MSE Programme Foundations: Principles of Economics 1, Principles of Economics 2, Mathematics for Economics, Further Mathematics for Economics. Effective August 2026: Principles of Economics, Math for Economics, Probability and Statistics.
- UG CGPA may be used in place of GRE/GMAT/SMU Admission Test scores for: **SMU alumni with CGPA 3.0/4.0 or above, within five years of graduation**; **NUS/NTU/SUTD/SUSS/SIT alumni with CGPA 3.5/5.0 or above, within five years of graduation**. Meeting the CGPA academic criteria listed above does not guarantee admission.
- Work experience is not mandatory.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content:
- Application documents include **GMAT / GRE / SMU Admission Test Score Report**.
- Admission Requirements include: **Good score in GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test**. _EQ: A very good score in the quantitative section will be expected_.
- UG CGPA may be used in place of GRE/GMAT/SMU Admission Test scores for the following applicants:
- SMU alumni with **CGPA 3.0/4.0 or above**, within five years of graduation.
- NUS/NTU/SUTD/SUSS/SIT alumni with **CGPA 3.5/5.0 or above**, within five years of graduation.
- _Note: Meeting the CGPA academic criteria listed above does not guarantee admission, and you may be advised to submit your GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test score to improve your chances of admission._
- The GMAT/GRE is recommended. However, if you have not taken the GMAT or GRE test, you may consider taking the online SMU Admission Test, which comprises three components: verbal, numerical, and inductive reasoning. Please click [Fact Sheet](https://economics.smu.edu.sg/sites/economics.smu.edu.sg/files/economics/MAE/SMU%20Admission%20Test%20Fact%20Sheet%20%28MSE%29.pdf) for information on SMU Admission Test registration and test details.
- If you intend to take the SMU Admission Test, please proceed to complete the MSE application first and make a payment of **S$125** in addition to the MSE application fee of **S$100**. Once you have completed payment for the test, send an email with your full name, application number and payment receipt to [mse@smu.edu.sg](mailto:mse@smu.edu.sg).
- For GMAT, we are looking for scores **600 or above**. For GRE, the verbal plus quantitative average should be **156 or above**. For SMU Admissions Test, the Verbal/Numerical/Integrated Reasoning average should be **55 or above**. For CAT, your score should put you into the **80th percentile or above**. Note that these are not hard cut-offs. We look at your overall application to see if you are a suitable candidate for us. We can accept students who fall below one or more of these minimums if there are positives in the application that compensate. Finally, we only need one of GRE/GMAT/SMUAT/CAT.
- Must I take the GRE/GMAT? For most applicants, yes. UG CGPA may be used in place of GRE/GMAT/SMU Admission Test scores for the following applicants: SMU alumni with **CGPA 3.0/4.0 or above**, within **5 years of graduation**; NUS/NTU/SUTD/SUSS/SIT alumni with **CGPA 3.5/5.0 or above**, within **5 years of graduation**. Note: Meeting the CGPA academic criteria listed above does not guarantee admission, and candidates may be recommended to submit GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test scores if it is felt this would improve chances of admission.
- Can I apply for the programme before taking GMAT/GRE? Yes, you can submit your application prior to taking the GMAT/GRE. Once you have completed your online application, an officer from our admissions team will get in touch with you within a month to advise you on the next steps, including the submission deadline for your GMAT/GRE exam scores.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
- IELTS / TOEFL is **required if your degree was not taught in English**.
- Admission requirements include: **Good TOEFL or IELTS (required if your first degree was not taught in English)**.
- For TOEFL and IELTS, your score should be **90 / 6.5 or above**. These are not hard cut-offs; the programme looks at the overall application and can accept students who fall below one or more of these minimums if there are positives in the application that compensate.
- TOEFL or IELTS is required only if your first degree is not in English.

Program Overview.content:
- The Master of Science in Economics (MSE), with tracks in Applied Economics (AE), Econometrics and Quantitative Economics (EQ), offers in-depth study of economics and economic data analysis. It includes an entry pathway for students without prior training in economics.
- The MSE is available for part-time or full-time study. Full-time study is 18 months, with flexibility to complete in 12 months; part-time study is 30 months, with flexibility to complete in 24 months. Maximum candidature is 2.5 years for full-time students and 4 years for part-time students.
- Effective August 2026 intake, the August intake will be open to students from diverse academic backgrounds, with foundation courses provided to bridge knowledge gaps. Students with strong quantitative backgrounds may be exempted from these courses and complete the programme in 12 months through the accelerated pathway, available in both August and January intakes.
- Students follow a strong core programme and a track system that allows a more practice-oriented focus or a more data-analytic and theoretical focus, along with an open category that allows courses outside the chosen track or from other programmes.
- The Applied Economics track is for working professionals who make or will make critical and strategic decisions in companies or public sector agencies and who can benefit from a good understanding of the market and the economy. It gives a comprehensive understanding of global economic issues for strategic decision making in the public sector and corporate world.
- The Econometrics and Quantitative Economics track is for students who wish to learn more about data analysis with a special focus on economic, financial and social data, pursue careers involving technical economics research, or pursue further graduate study in Economics. It focuses on modern and rigorous data analysis methods and covers economic theory, practice and research.
- The MSE programme features a strong yet flexible core, tracks that sharpen students’ focus, and a wide range of electives in the chosen track. Students may also take courses outside their track or programme for a personalised programme.
- The MSE is a 15 course unit (CU) programme with internship opportunities. Its structure comprises Foundations, Core, Electives, Open, and PGPD components; effective August 2026, the structure will be Foundation (3CUs), Core (3CUs), Elective (5CUs), Open (3CUs), and PGPD (1CU).
- The Foundations component is intended for students from non-Economics backgrounds who do not have the necessary training in economic theory and advanced quantitative techniques required by the MSE. Students with strong economics knowledge and advanced quantitative techniques are exempted from this component.
- The MSE Core equips students with rigorous knowledge in microeconomics, macroeconomics, and econometrics, providing the analytical framework on which sub-areas of economics are built.
- The Open component gives students flexibility to take courses from any MSE track/MSFE electives. Up to 1CU may be taken from pre-approved electives from other SMU Masters programmes. Students may choose to do a 10-week internship or a capstone project that satisfies a 1CU requirement.
- From the AY2021/22 intake onwards, internship will be a graduation requirement. Full-time students are required to complete a minimum 10-week internship in the April Term; students unable to take up a credit-bearing internship may seek approval to arrange an equivalent replacement such as a Capstone Project or electives.
- Average age in the class profile is 22 - 31 yrs, with gender profile 45.8(M) : 54.2(F), based on Classes of 2018-2021 (Full-time & Part-time).
- Industries MSE graduates work in include Business / Financial Services (19%), Consulting (13%), Investment / Securities (10%), Education (10%), Public Sector (8%), Healthcare (8%), Fintech (6%), Telecommunications (4%), Manufacturing (4%), and Others (18%), based on Classes of 2018-2020 (Full-time).
- Students will learn from frontline researchers, teaching specialists, industry practitioners and professionals.
- SMU has an internal online job portal for students to search and apply for internships and jobs. Students are assigned a dedicated career coach to provide career advisory and prepare them for internship and job placement.
- Careers after the MSc Econ include banks, investment banks, consultancies, insurance companies, government and regulatory agencies, education, research, business and HR, marketing, and related fields. Students on the Econometrics & Quantitative Economics track can also pursue careers as data scientists/analysts.

Curriculum.content:
- **Duration / study mode:** August / January intake. **18 Months Full-Time** with flexibility to complete in **12 months**; **30 Months Part-Time** with flexibility to complete in **24 months**. The MSc in Economics is available for part-time or full-time study. Maximum candidature is **2.5 years for full-time students**, and **4 years for part-time students**.
- August, January and April are regular **12-week terms**. November and July are optional **5-week terms**. Part-time students take **1-3 CU per regular term**; full-time students take **2-5 CU per regular term**.
- **Programme calendar:** **AY2026-2027** [download](https://economics.smu.edu.sg/sites/economics.smu.edu.sg/files/economics/PG_Doc/PG%20Academic%20Calendars%20(BRC%20Programmes)%20AY2026-27.pdf); **AY2025-2026** [download](https://economics.smu.edu.sg/sites/economics.smu.edu.sg/files/economics/PG_Doc/PG%20Academic%20Calendars%20(BRC%20Programmes)%20AY2025-26.pdf); **AY2024-2025** [download](https://economics.smu.edu.sg/sites/economics.smu.edu.sg/files/economics/PG_Doc/PG%20Academic%20Calendars%20(BRC%20Programmes)%20AY2024-25.pdf).
- The Master of Science in Economics (MSE) programme features a strong yet flexible core, tracks that sharpen your focus and a wide range of electives in your chosen track. Students may take courses outside of their track or programme for a personalised programme.
- Tracks: **Applied Economics Track** is available full-time or part-time. **Econometrics and Quantitative Economics Track** is full-time, with part-time option if able to take weekday daytime classes. Part-time study is available only to Singapore-based students: citizens, permanent residents, and those holding valid employment passes.
- **Programme Curriculum:** The MSE is a **15 course unit (CU)** programme with internship opportunities. Current structure: **Foundations (4CU), Core (3CU), Electives (5CU), Open (2CU), PGPD (1CU)**. Each course unit comprises ten 3-hour sessions. The academic requirement for graduation is a **Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of at least 2.50 out of 4.00**.
- Effective August 2026, the curriculum structure will be updated to: **Foundation (3CUs), Core (3CUs), Elective (5CUs), Open (3CUs), PGPD (1CU)**. The foundation component will be reduced by **1 CU**, and the open component increased by **1**, allowing for more flexibility and personalization.
- **Foundations:** Intended for students from non-Economics backgrounds who do not have the necessary training in economic theory and advanced quantitative techniques required by the MSE. Students with strong economics knowledge and advanced quantitative techniques are exempted from this component. Foundation courses listed: Principles of Economics 1, Principles of Economics 2, Mathematics for Economics, Further Mathematics for Economics. Effective August 2026 foundation courses listed: Principles of Economics, Math for Economics, Probability and Statistics.
- **Core (3CU):** Microeconomic Analysis, Macroeconomic Analysis, Econometric Analysis. EQ track students may apply to take PhD-level equivalent courses.
- **Track Electives (5CU):** Choose **5CU from the single track** to attain track status. Not all courses are available every year; course titles and content are subject to change and new courses are added from time to time.
- **Applied Economics Track courses:** Health Economics; Money, Banking, and International Finance; Macroeconomic Accounts and Public Finance; Economics of Growth, Poverty and Inequality; Politics, Institutions, and Economics; International Trade: Theory and Policy; Behavioural Economics; Infrastructure Economics and Policy; Environmental Economics; Economics of Competition Law; Spatial Econometrics and Data Analysis.
- **Econometrics and Quantitative Economics Track courses:** Spatial Econometrics and Data Analysis; Time Series Econometrics; Data Sampling; Panel Econometrics and Data Analysis; Machine Learning in Economics and Finance; Financial Econometrics; Continuous Time Financial Economics and Econometrics; Mathematical Methods for Economic Dynamics; Advanced Microeconomic Analysis; Empirical Industrial Economics; Macroeconomics 1 PhD; Selection of PhD Advanced Research Topics (ARTs).
- **Open (2CU):** Students may take courses from any MSE track/MSFE electives. Up to **1CU** may be taken from pre-approved electives from other SMU Masters programmes. Students may choose to do a **10-week internship** or a **capstone project** that satisfies a **1CU** requirement. The Open component will expand to **3CU effective August 2026**.
- Full-time students are encouraged to complete a minimum **10-week internship**. If unable to take up a credit-bearing internship, students may arrange an equivalent replacement such as a **Capstone Project or electives**. Full-time students may choose to complete a minimum of 10 weeks internship to satisfy **1CU** requirement under the open course category; students who do not wish to take up a credit-bearing internship may choose courses from any MSE track/MSFE electives, a capstone project, or up to **1CU** from pre-approved electives from other SMU Masters programmes.

Financial Aid.content:
SOE MSE Academic Merit Scholarship
- **Benefits:** The Merit 1 Scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$8,000 (inclusive of GST)**. The Merit 2 Scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$4,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility criteria:** Outstanding applicants to the MSE are eligible for the Merit Scholarships. The scholarship offer is conditional on matriculation into the MSE, i.e., the scholarship awardee must matriculate into the programme in order for the scholarship to be disbursed. Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void.
- **Exclusions:** You must not be a concurrent recipient of any other SMU-funded scholarship.
- **Application Process:** All applicants are automatically considered for the scholarship; no additional application is required.
SOE MSE Diversity Scholarship
- **Benefits:** The scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$8,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility criteria:** SOE Applicants with good academic backgrounds and who are citizens of countries that are underrepresented in the programme are eligible for the SOE MSE Diversity Scholarship. The scholarship awardee must matriculate into the MSE programme in order for the scholarship to be disbursed. Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void.
- **Exclusions:** You must not be a concurrent recipient of any other SMU-funded scholarship.
- **Application Process:** All eligible applicants are automatically considered for the scholarship; no additional application is required.
SMU ASEAN PG Scholarship
- **Benefits:** The scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$10,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility criteria:** The scholarship is open to citizens of ASEAN member countries or observer nations (PNG and Timor-Leste). The recipient must matriculate into the MSE programme to receive the award (no deferment of studies beyond the financial year of the award).
- **Exclusions:** You must not be a concurrent recipient of any other SMU-funded scholarship.
- **Application Process:** All eligible applicants are automatically considered for the scholarship; no additional application is required.
Roberto S. Mariano Best MSE Student Award
- **Benefits:** The award comprises a monetary award of **S$1,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Exclusions:** All graduating students are eligible.
Financing Options
- Scholarships and Outstanding Student Awards are available for deserving students.
- SkillsFuture Funding for Singapore Citizens. Click [here](https://www.skillsfuture.gov.sg/credit) for more details.
- Singapore Citizens with eligible Post Secondary Education Account (PSEA) may utilize balance funds for tuition fees. Click [here](https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/psea) for more details.
Discounts
- **Alumni Discount:** SMU and SUTD alumni are eligible for a discount of **$5,000** when applying to the MSE programme.
FAQ: “I see from your website you have scholarships ranging from $4,000 to $10,000. How do I apply?” You don’t have to. All eligible applicants will be considered for the appropriate scholarship, and informed when the offer is made. If you have an external scholarship and do not require a scholarship from us, please let us know.

Multiple Applications.content:
Must I indicate a track when I apply? Yes, and if admitted, your admission will be to a specific track of the program. Switching tracks is possible, but only with the School’s permission, and only if done early enough (before the main programme starts). Occasionally, the admission committee may feel that you are more suited to another track than to the one you applied to. In that case, they may suggest to you to consider the other track instead.
Can I apply for multiple tracks? Yes and no. The application system will ask you to choose a track. You may, however, indicate in your personal statement that you are willing to consider another track, or want to be considered for both tracks. We will channel your application to the appropriate track should you not get your first choice track.
Can I apply for multiple programmes? E.g., both MSE and MSFE? Yes.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
I’ve received an offer, but would like to defer my admission to the next intake. Is this possible? Yes it is, but you will have to pay the **$5000 (inclusive of GST) acceptance fee** in order to secure your place. Otherwise the offer will lapse and you will have to re-apply and be re-considered.
Scholarship conditions: Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void. For the SMU ASEAN PG Scholarship, the recipient must matriculate into the MSE programme to receive the award (**no deferment of studies beyond the financial year of the award**).
